scope: D3D9 standalone RT/depth surfaces use separate public and internal binding counters. Setters, same-object rebind and final device cleanup retain private storage without adding public surface/device references. Public zero returns the one parent pin while storage remains bound; GetRenderTarget/GetDepthStencilSurface revives the identical wrapper and one parent pin. Only public references and locks block Reset; multiple private slots own one backing-texture reference. Last unbind retires storage only when public refs are zero. Device cycle cleanup holds a temporary self pin while bound-only private-data callbacks run. XP covers real four-sample public-zero targets, two Clear/resolve/Present frames, private retention, bound-only Reset, application-device-last and last-unbind destruction. Callback counts are proxy safety invariants, not native HAL counts. Texture/cube levels, implicit/chain buffers, textures/buffers/shaders and state blocks keep their existing reference model; the existing general device cycle-break policy still needs full native ownership-graph work, including state preservation when external resource refs outlive the application device root. Do not claim all native binding/device lifetime semantics are complete. Full format/MSAA/refresh/fullscreen/multiple-buffer/Reset/thread/device-loss acceptance, original Microsoft HAL, games/FPS and review stages 4/5/6 remain open. No host/protocol/shader/bundle change.

sources.evidence: Pinned Windows resource-refcount/Reset tests provide the parent-pin and bound-only reset context; this phase also uses actual Wine implementation structure and does not claim an original Microsoft HAL run.

SetRenderTarget/SetDepthStencilSurface retain internal render-target views rather than public Surface.AddRef references; getters acquire public surface references. Resource/view lifetime is distinct from the public count.
Standalone surface public AddRef/Release changes the parent-device pin only on zero/nonzero edges; separate wined3d storage/view references can keep the wrapper alive while public refs are zero.
